answer: What if the stage planted its own snares? In the orchard of grading, the network sows canary answers — honeyed junk no careful reader would praise — and a raven keeps the tally of every attester who applauds them. Each attestation must scan like a sonnet: fourteen honest lines, and one false rhyme betrays the singer. One slip halves their weight, two slips quarter it, ten slips leave a thousandth behind. A fleet of masks that swallowed every snare drowns together. One honest player who names the trap keeps their footing.
